findings.issue_text: Removal-event cleanup in AdminPermissions.registerListener is now gated behind the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag, so permission resources/policies for deleted clients/roles/groups are no longer cleaned up when the feature is disabled, leaving orphaned authorization data (P2)

No V2 cleanup path exists when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled: the listener is gated off and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client with V2 permissions leaves orphaned resources and scope-permission policies in the realm resource server (P2)

ClientPermissionsV2 methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException on interface methods with live callers such as token-exchange evaluation and the client permissions admin endpoints; any un-gated caller will get an unhandled exception and HTTP 500 instead of a proper decision or clean 'not supported' response (P2)

ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission can return the "Clients" type resource name as a sentinel entry in the granted set instead of a client UUID when an all-clients permission grants, violating the set's contract that it contains client ids and potentially misbehaving for callers that inspect the set non-membership-wise (P3)

V2 evaluator throws UnsupportedOperationException from ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup path — client/role/group deletion may break or leave stale authorization resources when FGAP is enabled, because the listener is guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) which routes to the throwing ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled

canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles dropped the implicit grants present in V1 (no canManage(client) fallback and canMapCompositeRoles no longer implies canMapRoles), causing a behavior regression where admins with manage-clients get 403 on mapping client roles to users

Token-exchange and client permission-management paths (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, resource, getPermissions, setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException, producing 500 errors instead of proper denials for still-reachable call paths

Permission evaluation read path (hasPermission(ClientModel, String)) mutates the authorization store by creating the 'Clients' type resource via getResourceTypeResource when no per-client resource exists, risking race conditions with duplicate type resources and database resource pollution — inconsistent with the type-level hasPermission which returns false without creating anything

Per-resource policy evaluation loop (N+1 authorization evaluations) in getClientsWithPermission: iterates every Clients resource and runs a full evaluatePermission per resource, with root.realmResourceServer() re-fetched per resource and resource.getScopes() triggering a scope-load per resource, causing O(N clients × (policy lookups + scope loads + evaluation)) DB operations per invocation on the client listing path

Per-call findByName + full evaluatePermission in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) for each check (canConfigure, canManage, canView, canMapRoles, etc.) with no batching or memoization, plus cascading evaluations (canView → canConfigure → canManage) that re-evaluate the same resource up to 3× per client

getClientsWithPermission eagerly materializes the full grant set without pagination, store-level filtering, or short-circuiting: it scans all Clients-type resources even when most have no permission resource at all, so cost scales with total clients rather than granted clients

P1: V2 permission evaluator methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource(ClientModel), getPermissions(ClientModel)) throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning deny-by-default (false/empty result), causing reachable code paths like token-exchange evaluation to surface HTTP 500 instead of a clean 403

P2: Deletion-cleanup ProviderEventListener in AdminPermissions is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which doesn't match the V2 activation condition — when only the V2 feature is enabled the listener no-ops, orphaning per-client Resource entries for deleted clients/roles/groups forever

P2: If V1 and V2 flags can co-occur, the cleanup listener invokes ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException, turning client/role/group deletion into a 500 error

P2: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 iterates only per-client CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources and ignores type-level (all-clients) grants, returning an empty/partial client list for admins who hold an all-clients grant — the per-client and type-level grant paths should be unioned

P3: canViewClientScopes() and canListClientScopes() are not overridden in ClientPermissionsV2, so schema-level VIEW/MANAGE grants on 'Clients' don't extend to realm-level client-scope endpoints, causing inconsistent 403s for legitimately-granted users

Cleanup-on-removal listener in AdminPermissions is silently skipped when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag is off, orphaning permission resources/policies for removed clients/roles/groups and causing stale permissions to resurface after a feature toggle cycle

ClientPermissionsV2 throws bare UnsupportedOperationException from ~10 inherited ClientPermissionEvaluator/ClientPermissionManagement methods, causing existing admin REST endpoints (isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled, canExchangeTo) to surface HTTP 500 errors instead of meaningful 4xx responses when V2 is enabled

Test cleanup lambdas in AbstractPermissionTest (createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy helpers) lack a null check on findByName, causing NPE in cleanup that masks the original failure and can leak client-scoped authorization resources

AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient returns null for invalid client IDs and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission has no error path for deleted clients, so under V2 (where removal cleanup doesn't run) deleted clients leave stale queryable permission resources that still appear in admin listings

P1: Client/role/group removal cleanup path changed: setPermissionsEnabled call is now gated behind ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag; when enabled, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client with the feature enabled may fail at runtime

P1: When the feature flag is disabled, stale V1 permission resources are no longer cleaned up on entity removal, and neither cleanup path (feature enabled or disabled) has any test coverage in this PR

P2: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and canMapClientScopeRoles implementation have zero test coverage — no test verifies granting the scope enables client-scope role-mapping or that it is denied without the grant

P2: resolveClient's getClientByClientId fallback (resolution by clientId instead of internal UUID) is never tested; all tests pass myclient.getId(), leaving resolution-by-clientId and the create-resource-with-name path unverified

P2: V2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles drop the admin-role (hasOneAdminRole) shortcut and return only hasPermission, a potential silent regression for admins holding MANAGE_CLIENTS; no test pins down intended behavior for admin-role holders

P2: No negative (Logic.NEGATIVE) permission tests for the Clients resource type; deny-permission overriding an all-clients grant (the scenario hasPermission's fallback branch handles) is untested, only POSITIVE logic is exercised

P3: Scope-validation matrix in PermissionRESTTest.permissionsTest not extended for the new Clients type; BAD_REQUEST cases (missing resourceType, missing/non-existent scopes) still only use USERS, and rejection of V1 scopes like 'impersonate' for Clients is never validated

P3: Twelve V1 methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, managePermission, getPermissions, etc.) now throw UnsupportedOperationException with no test verifying how these surface over REST when the feature is enabled (4xx/405 vs 500) or that V1-only endpoints are hidden
P3: getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2 (~line 260) is dead code, indicating the token-exchange wiring was dropped mid-implementation without a test documenting the intended V2 behavior

Dead code: unused private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) in ClientPermissionsV2.java (~267) has no callers since canExchangeTo is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException; keeps ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports alive unnecessarily

Triplicated permission-evaluation loop in ClientPermissionsV2.java (~231–250, ~252–270, ~278–286): three near-identical blocks building ResourcePermission and evaluating permissions, with scope matching obscured by Arrays.asList(scope) instead of direct equals, and likely duplicated with UserPermissionsV2 — changes to evaluation semantics must be replicated in 3+ places

Feature-flag gate in AdminPermissions.java (~77) wraps all removal cleanup (RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent → setPermissionsEnabled(false)) inside Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ); if the feature is disabled after permissions were created, deleting roles/clients/groups leaves orphaned authorization data that resurfaces on re-enable, and the profile concern is mixed into the event listener instead of the permission managers

Fragile partial-subclass: ClientPermissionsV2 extends the V1 ClientPermissions and overrides ~12 V1 methods to throw UnsupportedOperationException while inheriting the rest of V1 behavior; any inherited unoverridden method silently executes V1 logic and new interface methods compile fine but blow up at runtime (e.g., a 500 instead of a denial)

Wrong/misleading javadoc on ClientPermissionEvaluator.java (~70): requireView() is a void throwing method that guards canView(), but is documented as 'Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true'; requireViewClientScopes() similarly says 'Returns true' for a void method

Test helper cleanup lambdas in AbstractPermissionTest.java (~124, ~138) (createUserPolicy, createClientPolicy) dereference findByName(name).getId() without a null check; if the removal-time lookup fails, the cleanup lambda throws an NPE that can mask the real test result or leave residue

Growing type-string dispatch in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (~90–95, ~175): getOrCreateResource resolves names via an if/else chain on resource type, and each new type adds constants, a set, an if-branch, and a resolveX(session, id) method; a resolver-per-type map or per-ResourceType hook would keep adding types O(1)

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only the instance resource if it exists, falling back to the type resource, but never both together — causing false denies when an all-clients grant is ignored due to an existing instance resource, and a deny-bypass where a NEGATIVE all-clients permission on the 'Clients' type resource is never seen when a specific resource carries a POSITIVE grant (the same flaw exists in UserPermissionsV2)

AdminPermissions.onEvent wraps role/client/group removal cleanup (setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) — with the flag off, legacy V1 cleanup no longer runs (silent regression producing orphaned authorization data); with the flag on, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and there is no V2 cleanup path at all, so deleting entities with V2 permission resources leaves stale resources and policies permanently in the database

ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission may include the 'Clients' type resource in the granted set because resourceStore.findByType matches by type attribute and the type resource itself has type 'Clients' — the literal type-resource name (not a client id) is added to a set whose contract is client ids, potentially yielding wrong/empty filtering results for admins with purely type-level grants

ClientPermissionsV2 leaves a dozen inherited interface methods (setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, exchangeToPermission, canExchangeTo, etc.) throwing UnsupportedOperationException, which are reachable from admin endpoints under V2 (e.g., legacy per-client management/permissions endpoint, token-exchange checks invoking canExchangeTo) — surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of a proper 4xx; canExchangeTo failing with an exception instead of returning a deny changes token-exchange failure mode from 'denied' to 'server error' and is exploitable as a denial vector

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal-event cleanup in AdminPermissions.registerListener is now gated behind the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag, so permission resources/policies for deleted clients/roles/groups are no longer cleaned up when the feature is disabled, leaving orphaned authorization data (P2)

No V2 cleanup path exists when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled: the listener is gated off and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client with V2 permissions leaves orphaned resources and scope-permission policies in the realm resource server (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` where `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` (now gated under `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`). If the V2 management implementation is in effect (`MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`), client deletion will trigger this listener and throw at runtime instead of performing the intended cleanup/disable logic, which can reasonably leave authz artifacts (resources/policies) behind. The finding’s mention of the specific V2 feature flag name can’t be verified from the diff, but the exception-on-cleanup path is directly evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException on interface methods with live callers such as token-exchange evaluation and the client permissions admin endpoints; any un-gated caller will get an unhandled exception and HTTP 500 instead of a proper decision or clean 'not supported' response (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2` a number of overridden methods (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `mapRolesClientScopePermission`, `mapRolesCompositePermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. The diff does not show any explicit guard at the call sites to ensure these methods are never invoked when `ClientPermissionsV2` is in use (e.g., by REST/admin endpoints or token-exchange paths). While the finding’s claim about “live callers” can’t be verified from this diff alone, the introduced `UnsupportedOperationException` implementations are a concrete, diff-grounded risk that could surface as runtime failures if any code path reaches them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission can return the "Clients" type resource name as a sentinel entry in the granted set instead of a client UUID when an all-clients permission grants, violating the set's contract that it contains client ids and potentially misbehaving for callers that inspect the set non-membership-wise (P3)

V2 evaluator throws UnsupportedOperationException from ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup path — client/role/group deletion may break or leave stale authorization resources when FGAP is enabled, because the listener is guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) which routes to the throwing ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled

canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles dropped the implicit grants present in V1 (no canManage(client) fallback and canMapCompositeRoles no longer implies canMapRoles), causing a behavior regression where admins with manage-clients get 403 on mapping client roles to users

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new V2 overrides in `ClientPermissionsV2` where `canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles` simply call `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` and do not fall back to `canManage(client)` or to admin roles. However, the finding’s core claim—that this is a regression from V1 where MANAGE_CLIENTS implicitly granted these operations (and that composite mapping implied basic role mapping)—is not verifiable from this PR diff because no V1 implementation is shown, and the updated `ClientPermissionEvaluator` Javadoc for these methods does not state any MANAGE_CLIENTS fallback or composite→map-roles implication. So the asserted “dropped implicit grants present in V1”/“admins with manage-clients now get 403” behavior change cannot be confirmed purely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token-exchange and client permission-management paths (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, resource, getPermissions, setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException, producing 500 errors instead of proper denials for still-reachable call paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes these UnsupportedOperationException paths reachable. In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). MgmtPermissionsV2 now overrides clients() to return a ClientPermissionsV2 instance, whose setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). This would trigger a runtime exception during client removal handling (likely resulting in a 500 / error), instead of a proper no-op/denial/cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission evaluation read path (hasPermission(ClientModel, String)) mutates the authorization store by creating the 'Clients' type resource via getResourceTypeResource when no per-client resource exists, risking race conditions with duplicate type resources and database resource pollution — inconsistent with the type-level hasPermission which returns false without creating anything

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, when no per-client resource exists it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` (commented as loading the "all-clients" resource) and then checks policies; this differs from the type-level `hasPermission(String)` which simply `findByName(...)` and returns `false` if missing. If `getResourceTypeResource` is a create-or-get helper (as the name suggests in this codebase), this introduces a side-effecting code path during permission evaluation (potentially creating the Clients-type resource even when no policy exists). However, the diff doesn’t show `getResourceTypeResource`’s implementation, so the store-mutation/race/pollution claim can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-resource policy evaluation loop (N+1 authorization evaluations) in getClientsWithPermission: iterates every Clients resource and runs a full evaluatePermission per resource, with root.realmResourceServer() re-fetched per resource and resource.getScopes() triggering a scope-load per resource, causing O(N clients × (policy lookups + scope loads + evaluation)) DB operations per invocation on the client listing path

adjudication.rationale: The new method `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` iterates all resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and, for each resource, calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`. That helper performs a full `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), ...)` per resource and also re-fetches `ResourceServer server = root.realmResourceServer()` inside the helper (even though the outer method already computed `server`). This is inherently O(N resources) authorization evaluations, and `resource.getScopes()` may trigger per-resource scope loading depending on store implementation. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/N+1 concern, but not a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-call findByName + full evaluatePermission in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) for each check (canConfigure, canManage, canView, canMapRoles, etc.) with no batching or memoization, plus cascading evaluations (canView → canConfigure → canManage) that re-evaluate the same resource up to 3× per client

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, most access checks (`canManage(ClientModel)`, `canConfigure(ClientModel)`, `canView(ClientModel)`, `canMapRoles*`) call `hasPermission(client, scope)`, which performs a `resourceStore.findByName(...)` lookup and then calls `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))` each time. Additionally, `canConfigure(client)` calls `canManage(client)` first, and `canView(client)` calls `canConfigure(client)` (and `canView()`), so a single `canView(client)` path can trigger multiple `hasPermission(...)` evaluations for the same client (e.g., MANAGE then CONFIGURE, plus potentially VIEW). The diff shows no memoization/batching to avoid repeated store lookups and permission evaluations, making this a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by this change rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission eagerly materializes the full grant set without pagination, store-level filtering, or short-circuiting: it scans all Clients-type resources even when most have no permission resource at all, so cost scales with total clients rather than granted clients

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)`, the code iterates *all* authorization resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each calls `hasGrantedPermission(...)`, which triggers `root.evaluatePermission(...)`. There is no pagination, store-level filtering by scope/policy, or early exit; it always scans the full set of `Clients`-type resources present in the authz store. This is a real performance/scalability concern introduced by the diff, but it is not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: V2 permission evaluator methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource(ClientModel), getPermissions(ClientModel)) throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning deny-by-default (false/empty result), causing reachable code paths like token-exchange evaluation to surface HTTP 500 instead of a clean 403

That is a concrete, diff-grounded concern because if any code path invokes these methods under V2 it will fail hard rather than deny-by-default. However, the finding’s claim that these are reachable (e.g., “token-exchange evaluation”) and would surface as HTTP 500 cannot be verified from the provided diff alone (no call sites shown), so it’s not a verifiable defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds schema-level permissions for Clients in V2 (e.g., ClientPermissionsV2.canView() / canManage() / canManageClientScopes() now consult AdminPermissionsSchema scopes), but ClientPermissionsV2 does not override the realm-level client-scope gate methods declared on ClientPermissionEvaluator (canViewClientScopes(), canListClientScopes(), requireListClientScopes()). From the diff alone we can verify those methods are not overridden in ClientPermissionsV2, so whether schema-level VIEW/MANAGE on the Clients resource type applies to client-scope listing/viewing depends entirely on how the inherited ClientPermissions implementations are written (not shown). That creates a concrete risk of inconsistent authorization behavior if the base methods don’t delegate to the overridden V2 methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cleanup-on-removal listener in AdminPermissions is silently skipped when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag is off, orphaning permission resources/policies for removed clients/roles/groups and causing stale permissions to resurface after a feature toggle cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissions.registerListener() to wrap *all* cleanup handling (RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent) in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` was invoked unconditionally on these removal events. With this change, when the feature flag is off the listener does nothing, so any existing fine-grained authz artifacts associated with removed roles/clients/groups will not be disabled/cleaned up via these calls, which matches the finding’s core claim that cleanup is silently skipped when the flag is off.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 throws bare UnsupportedOperationException from ~10 inherited ClientPermissionEvaluator/ClientPermissionManagement methods, causing existing admin REST endpoints (isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled, canExchangeTo) to surface HTTP 500 errors instead of meaningful 4xx responses when V2 is enabled

adjudication.rationale: In the added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, multiple inherited methods are overridden to immediately `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, and several `*Permission(...)` methods). The diff also wires V2 into runtime via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning a `ClientPermissionsV2` instance. Since these are runtime methods (not test-only) and the exceptions are unchecked and not translated to a JAX-RS/Keycloak-specific 4xx, any code path that invokes them under V2 will fail with an unhandled runtime exception (typically surfacing as HTTP 500). The diff itself shows at least one such reachable call site pattern: the admin permissions event listener calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`; if `management(...)` resolves to V2 when the feature is enabled, that will now throw `UnsupportedOperationException` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup lambdas in AbstractPermissionTest (createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy helpers) lack a null check on findByName, causing NPE in cleanup that masks the original failure and can leak client-scoped authorization resources

adjudication.rationale: In AbstractPermissionTest, the new helpers createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy register cleanup lambdas that unconditionally do `...findByName(name).getId()` (e.g., `policies().user().findByName(name).getId()`), with no null check. If the policy cannot be found at cleanup time (e.g., creation partially failed, name collision, policy removed/renamed by the test), `findByName(name)` can be null and cleanup will throw NPE, potentially masking the original test failure and preventing cleanup of related authz artifacts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient returns null for invalid client IDs and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission has no error path for deleted clients, so under V2 (where removal cleanup doesn't run) deleted clients leave stale queryable permission resources that still appear in admin listings

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2 but leaves lifecycle/cleanup operations unimplemented: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException. Yet AdminPermissions.registerListener() (now gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) still calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent. With MgmtPermissionsV2 now overriding clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, client-removal cleanup in V2 will not run (it will throw), so any existing authz resources for that client (queried via resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) in getClientsWithPermission) can remain and be returned without any check that the underlying client still exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Client/role/group removal cleanup path changed: setPermissionsEnabled call is now gated behind ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag; when enabled, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client with the feature enabled may fail at runtime

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent. The diff adds MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, under the V2 permissions path, client-removal cleanup will raise a runtime exception when it tries to disable permissions for the removed client.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: When the feature flag is disabled, stale V1 permission resources are no longer cleaned up on entity removal, and neither cleanup path (feature enabled or disabled) has any test coverage in this PR

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the entire entity-removal cleanup logic (for `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, `GroupRemovedEvent`) was previously unconditional but is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. When the feature flag is disabled, the listener now performs no cleanup at all, so any previously-created admin-permissions artifacts (e.g., resources/policies tied to removed roles/clients/groups) will no longer be disabled/cleaned via `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`. The added/modified tests in this diff focus on permission evaluation and CRUD of permissions, not on listener-driven cleanup on entity removal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and canMapClientScopeRoles implementation have zero test coverage — no test verifies granting the scope enables client-scope role-mapping or that it is denied without the grant

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and a corresponding evaluator method `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client)` that checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. However, the added/updated tests in `PermissionClientTest` cover `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (e.g., `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`) but do not grant or assert behavior for `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, nor do they exercise an endpoint that would require `canMapClientScopeRoles`. This is a specific missing-test gap for newly added authorization logic, not a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: resolveClient's getClientByClientId fallback (resolution by clientId instead of internal UUID) is never tested; all tests pass myclient.getId(), leaving resolution-by-clientId and the create-resource-with-name path unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new resolution logic for CLIENTS resources in `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(...)`, including a fallback from `session.clients().getClientById(realm, id)` to `session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id)`. In the added/modified tests (e.g., `PermissionClientTest`), permissions are created using `myclient.getId()` (internal UUID) as the resource identifier (e.g., `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, ...)`). There is no test that creates a permission/resource using the public `clientId` string (e.g., "myclient"), so the fallback branch and the "create resource with name resolved from clientId" behavior in `getOrCreateResource` for `CLIENTS` are not exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: V2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles drop the admin-role (hasOneAdminRole) shortcut and return only hasPermission, a potential silent regression for admins holding MANAGE_CLIENTS; no test pins down intended behavior for admin-role holders

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `canMapRoles(ClientModel)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` are overridden to return only `hasPermission(client, ...)` (see `ClientPermissionsV2`), while other V2 methods (e.g., `canManage(ClientModel)` and `canManageClientScopes()`) explicitly preserve an `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS` shortcut via `root.hasOneAdminRole(...)`. This asymmetry is verifiable in the diff and could change behavior for callers who rely on admin roles alone to map roles, but the diff does not establish the intended semantics. The added tests (e.g., `PermissionClientTest#testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`) exercise permission-based grants and denials, but do not pin down expected behavior for an admin-role holder (e.g., `MANAGE_CLIENTS`) without corresponding authz permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No negative (Logic.NEGATIVE) permission tests for the Clients resource type; deny-permission overriding an all-clients grant (the scenario hasPermission's fallback branch handles) is untested, only POSITIVE logic is exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial client permission evaluation in `ClientPermissionsV2`, including a fallback path in `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` that evaluates the special "all-clients" resource when the per-client resource is missing (and only proceeds if there are policies attached to that resource). The new `PermissionClientTest` exercises only POSITIVE permissions via `createPermission(..., Set.of(...), policy)` and `createAllPermission(..., Set.of(...))`, and never uses the `Logic.NEGATIVE` overload for the Clients resource type. In contrast, negative-logic override behavior is explicitly tested for Users in `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` (e.g., `createPermission(client, Logic.NEGATIVE, ...)`). So the specific deny-overrides-all-clients-grant scenario is indeed untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Scope-validation matrix in PermissionRESTTest.permissionsTest not extended for the new Clients type; BAD_REQUEST cases (missing resourceType, missing/non-existent scopes) still only use USERS, and rejection of V1 scopes like 'impersonate' for Clients is never validated

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new resource type `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`/`CLIENTS` with new scopes (`CONFIGURE`, `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`) in `AdminPermissionsSchema`, and introduces substantial new evaluation logic in `ClientPermissionsV2`. However, `PermissionRESTTest.permissionsTest()` still only exercises BAD_REQUEST validation using `AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS.getType()` and user scopes; there are no analogous negative tests for `CLIENTS` (e.g., missing resourceType with client scopes, missing scopes with CLIENTS, invalid scopes for CLIENTS such as `impersonate`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in validation coverage for the newly added Clients type rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Twelve V1 methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, managePermission, getPermissions, etc.) now throw UnsupportedOperationException with no test verifying how these surface over REST when the feature is enabled (4xx/405 vs 500) or that V1-only endpoints are hidden

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, multiple inherited/overridden methods (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (`ClientPermissionsV2.java`, many `@Override` methods). The diff also adds/updates tests around V2 client permissions (e.g., `PermissionClientTest`) but none exercise these V1-style operations or assert that any REST endpoints invoking them are disabled/hidden or return an expected 4xx/405 rather than surfacing as a 500. This is a concrete, diff-grounded completeness/test-coverage concern, not a proven functional defect from the diff alone (since we can’t see whether REST paths still call these methods under V2).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2 (~line 260) is dead code, indicating the token-exchange wiring was dropped mid-implementation without a test documenting the intended V2 behavior

Dead code: unused private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) in ClientPermissionsV2.java (~267) has no callers since canExchangeTo is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException; keeps ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports alive unnecessarily
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that ClientPermissionsV2 defines a private getEvaluationContext(...) method that is never called (dead/unused code) and should be removed; candidate adds context about why it has no callers and mentions related unused imports, but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Triplicated permission-evaluation loop in ClientPermissionsV2.java (~231–250, ~252–270, ~278–286): three near-identical blocks building ResourcePermission and evaluating permissions, with scope matching obscured by Arrays.asList(scope) instead of direct equals, and likely duplicated with UserPermissionsV2 — changes to evaluation semantics must be replicated in 3+ places

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2.java`, there are three very similar permission-evaluation blocks: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` (builds a `ResourcePermission`, calls `root.evaluatePermission(...)`, then scans `permission.getScopes()` for a match), `hasPermission(String)` (same but for the all-clients resource), and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)` (same scanning logic). The scope check in the first two uses `List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope)` followed by `expectedScopes.contains(s)` even though only a single scope is ever checked, which obscures the intent and increases maintenance burden. This is a concrete, diff-grounded duplication/maintainability issue, not a correctness defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-flag gate in AdminPermissions.java (~77) wraps all removal cleanup (RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent → setPermissionsEnabled(false)) inside Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ); if the feature is disabled after permissions were created, deleting roles/clients/groups leaves orphaned authorization data that resurfaces on re-enable, and the profile concern is mixed into the event listener instead of the permission managers

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), the diff wraps all ProviderEvent cleanup handlers (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent -> setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously the cleanup ran unconditionally. With this change, if fine-grained authz was enabled (and thus authz resources/policies may exist) and later the feature is disabled, subsequent deletions of roles/clients/groups will no longer trigger cleanup, leaving authorization artifacts in the store. If the feature is later re-enabled, those stale artifacts could become effective again, which is a correctness/security-relevant behavioral regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile partial-subclass: ClientPermissionsV2 extends the V1 ClientPermissions and overrides ~12 V1 methods to throw UnsupportedOperationException while inheriting the rest of V1 behavior; any inherited unoverridden method silently executes V1 logic and new interface methods compile fine but blow up at runtime (e.g., a 500 instead of a denial)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a fragile design: `ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions` and explicitly overrides many inherited V1-oriented methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `setPermissionsEnabled`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, multiple `*Permission(...)` methods in `ClientPermissionsV2`). This creates a real risk that any unoverridden inherited behavior from `ClientPermissions` (or any caller expecting these API methods to work) will execute V1 logic or hit these UOEs at runtime. The risk is also concrete in this diff because `AdminPermissions.registerListener` calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`; if `management(...).clients()` resolves to `ClientPermissionsV2` (MgmtPermissionsV2 now overrides `clients()` to return it), that would throw at runtime. The diff alone doesn’t prove the selection logic for V2 vs V1 `management(...)`, so it’s not fully verifiable as an immediate defect, but the subclass/UOE pattern is clearly present and brittle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong/misleading javadoc on ClientPermissionEvaluator.java (~70): requireView() is a void throwing method that guards canView(), but is documented as 'Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true'; requireViewClientScopes() similarly says 'Returns true' for a void method

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionEvaluator.java, the newly added Javadocs for void guard methods are misleading: `requireView()` is declared `void` but its Javadoc says “Returns true if {@link #canView()} returns true”, and `requireViewClientScopes()` is also `void` but says “Returns true if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns true”. These should describe throwing ForbiddenException when the corresponding `can*` check is false (as other `require*` methods’ Javadocs do). The finding’s mention that `requireView()` references `canViewClientScopes()` is not shown in the diff (it references `canView()`), but the core issue (wrong ‘Returns true’ wording for void methods) is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test helper cleanup lambdas in AbstractPermissionTest.java (~124, ~138) (createUserPolicy, createClientPolicy) dereference findByName(name).getId() without a null check; if the removal-time lookup fails, the cleanup lambda throws an NPE that can mask the real test result or leave residue

adjudication.rationale: In AbstractPermissionTest.java the newly added cleanup lambdas in createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy do `...findByName(name).getId()` without checking whether `findByName(name)` returned null. The diff clearly shows this null-unsafe dereference inside delayed cleanup code, which could turn a cleanup-time lookup miss into an NPE and potentially mask earlier test failures or prevent cleanup from completing. Whether the lookup can actually fail isn’t proven by the diff alone, but the risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Growing type-string dispatch in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (~90–95, ~175): getOrCreateResource resolves names via an if/else chain on resource type, and each new type adds constants, a set, an if-branch, and a resolveX(session, id) method; a resolver-per-type map or per-ResourceType hook would keep adding types O(1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff extends AdminPermissionsSchema with a new resource type (CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE/CLIENTS) and correspondingly grows the type-based dispatch in getOrCreateResource: it adds an `else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType)) { name = resolveClient(session, id); }` branch and a new `resolveClient(...)` method. This matches the finding that each new resource type requires adding constants, a ResourceType, an if/else branch, and a resolver method. It’s a maintainability/architecture concern (string/type dispatch growth), not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only the instance resource if it exists, falling back to the type resource, but never both together — causing false denies when an all-clients grant is ignored due to an existing instance resource, and a deny-bypass where a NEGATIVE all-clients permission on the 'Clients' type resource is never seen when a specific resource carries a POSITIVE grant (the same flaw exists in UserPermissionsV2)

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first looks up a per-client resource (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`). If that resource exists, it evaluates permissions ONLY on that resource and never also evaluates the resource-type (“all-clients”) resource. The fallback to the type resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) happens only when the per-client resource is null. This means an all-clients grant/deny attached to the type resource can be ignored whenever an instance resource exists, matching the finding’s false-deny and deny-bypass scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.onEvent wraps role/client/group removal cleanup (setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) — with the flag off, legacy V1 cleanup no longer runs (silent regression producing orphaned authorization data); with the flag on, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and there is no V2 cleanup path at all, so deleting entities with V2 permission resources leaves stale resources and policies permanently in the database

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), the removal-event cleanup calls (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) are now wrapped inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`, whereas previously they always ran. This means when the feature flag is off, no cleanup runs at all (the old unconditional behavior is removed). Additionally, the new V2 implementation `ClientPermissionsV2` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)`, so if `management(...).clients()` resolves to the V2 permissions (as suggested by adding `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)`), the client removal event path would throw instead of cleaning up authorization data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission may include the 'Clients' type resource in the granted set because resourceStore.findByType matches by type attribute and the type resource itself has type 'Clients' — the literal type-resource name (not a client id) is added to a set whose contract is client ids, potentially yielding wrong/empty filtering results for admins with purely type-level grants
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both point out that getClientsWithPermission uses resourceStore.findByType on CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, which can include/return the type-level "Clients" resource and then adds resource.getName() (a literal resource name) into a set that is supposed to contain client IDs. This mismap can lead to incorrect behavior (e.g., realm.getClientById gets a non-ID and may return null/fail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 leaves a dozen inherited interface methods (setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, exchangeToPermission, canExchangeTo, etc.) throwing UnsupportedOperationException, which are reachable from admin endpoints under V2 (e.g., legacy per-client management/permissions endpoint, token-exchange checks invoking canExchangeTo) — surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of a proper 4xx; canExchangeTo failing with an exception instead of returning a deny changes token-exchange failure mode from 'denied' to 'server error' and is exploitable as a denial vector

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return a `ClientPermissionsV2` instance. `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides several inherited methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` and `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)`. Separately, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now wraps its event handling in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }` and within that block still invokes `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` for `ClientRemovedEvent`. Under V2, that call will hit `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` and throw, which would surface as an unhandled runtime exception during event processing (i.e., server error behavior). The broader claims about token-exchange/admin endpoints being reachable are not directly verifiable from this diff, but at least the `setPermissionsEnabled` path is clearly reachable from code shown.
